role.altitude: The surgical assistant keeps checking the patient, positioning and padding, judging skin and circulation and working with the surgeon; reading names off lists, phoning around for shared equipment and writing findings in free text shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping equipment bookings and preference cards current
role.ambitious_version: An assistant who knows before the first case that every item and device is there.

tasks.short: Scan the wristband against the OR list and record, ask the patient to confirm, check the site marking against consent and imaging, and verify the identity of patient and operative site in the team time-out.

steps.what: Surgical assistant compares the patient's wristband with the OR list and the record
Surgical assistant asks the patient to state name, date of birth and procedure
Surgical assistant checks the site marking against the consent and imaging
Surgical assistant verifies the identity of patient and operative site with the team in the time-out

tasks.design: Scanning the wristband barcode opens the patient's OR case and shows name, number, procedure, side and consent status side by side with the OR list, instead of the assistant reading and comparing them by hand. Asking the patient, checking the site marking and the team time-out stay fully with the people in the room; the scan supports the check and never replaces it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Names and numbers were read and compared by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Barcoded wristbands linked to the OR case in the record.
tasks.still_hard: Emergency patients without a wristband yet.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that the patient's answer and the marking do not match.

reach.learn: Whether mismatches are caught before the time-out.

evidence.claim: Barcoded wristbands scanned against the record are used for patient identification in hospitals.
Health data are a special category of personal data.

assumptions: Boundary: verifying identity and site before the procedure; discussing the procedure and consent with the surgeon (task 19296) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: wristbands with barcodes printed at admission by the ward, for about 95% of planned patients; s1 is priced at that share.
Asking, checking the marking and the time-out keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of patients with a scannable wristband on arrival in the OR.
research_questions: Do identity mismatches found at the time-out fall?

incremental.description: Surgical assistant reports unreadable wristbands to the ward.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many emergency patients; high: planned lists with scannable wristbands.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check the preference card, gather positioning equipment and protective padding, coordinate or participate in positioning the patient, check pressure points, and record position and padding.

steps.what: Surgical assistant checks the surgeon's preference card for position and equipment
Surgical assistant gathers positioning equipment and protective padding
Surgical assistant coordinates the team and positions the patient with body stabilizing equipment for exposure
Surgical assistant applies padding and checks pressure points, nerves and circulation
Surgical assistant records position and padding in the record

tasks.design: Nothing changes in the positioning itself: gathering equipment, positioning, padding and checking pressure points stay hands-on and keep their time. Position and padding are recorded with pick lists of standard positions and padded points in the OR record instead of free text.
tasks.previous_blocker: Position and padding were typed as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Pick lists in the OR record.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual positions not on the list.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that an arm is under strain before it shows.

evidence.claim: Structured pick lists in the record replace free-text entries.

assumptions: Boundary: positioning before the procedure; monitoring position during surgery (task 19300) is a sibling task.
s1 keeps its full time; finding preference cards is priced in task 19307.
Gathering, positioning and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether the OR record already has position pick lists.
research_questions: Are position records complete more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: pick lists already in use; high: free-text records today.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the day's cases and preference cards, check case carts and instruments, determine availability of shared equipment, decide on substitutes, and request missing supplies.

steps.what: Surgical assistant reads the OR schedule and preference cards for the necessary equipment and supplies
Surgical assistant checks the case cart and instruments in the OR
Surgical assistant determines availability of shared equipment such as imaging units and microscopes
Surgical assistant decides on substitutes and tells the surgeon about missing items
Surgical assistant requests missing supplies from the OR store or sterile services

tasks.design: The OR schedule in the record lists, per case, the items from the surgeon's digital preference card, instead of the assistant looking up each card in a binder. Shared equipment is booked per case in the OR planning system, so the assistant sees which room has the imaging unit or microscope instead of phoning around. Missing items are requested with a request form that shows status, instead of phoning the store. Checking the cart and deciding on substitutes stay with the assistant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preference cards were on paper and equipment was found by phoning.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital preference cards and equipment bookings in OR planning.
tasks.still_hard: Emergency cases added during the day.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which substitute this surgeon will accept.
tasks.altitude: Less phoning and looking up; checking stays.

reach.learn: Whether fewer items are missing at the start of a case.

evidence.claim: OR planning systems hold digital preference cards and equipment bookings per case.

assumptions: Boundary: determining availability before the case; positioning (task 19294) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: preference cards kept current in the record by the OR team leads, for about 80% of procedures; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3: all OR teams book shared equipment per case.
Checking the cart and deciding keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of shared devices per OR complex.
research_questions: Do delays from missing equipment fall?

incremental.description: Surgical assistant updates equipment bookings when the case order changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few shared devices and stable lists; high: many shared devices and frequent case changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Remove positioning equipment after completion of the procedure, assess skin integrity and other body conditions, record findings on a body map, and hand over to recovery.

steps.what: Surgical assistant removes padding and positioning equipment after completion of the procedure
Surgical assistant assesses skin integrity at pressure points
Surgical assistant checks other body conditions such as circulation and nerve function
Surgical assistant records any damage from positioning in the record
Surgical assistant hands over findings to the recovery nurse

tasks.design: Removing equipment, assessing the skin, checking circulation and nerves and the handover stay hands-on. Findings go on a body map with pick lists for location and grade in the OR record, instead of free text.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were written as free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Body maps with pick lists in the record.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle redness that fades within minutes.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a pressure mark from a burn or bruise.

reach.learn: Whether positioning injuries are followed up more consistently.

evidence.claim: Body maps with pick lists are common in nursing records.

assumptions: Boundary: assessing after the procedure; monitoring during surgery (task 19300) is a sibling task.
Removing, assessing, checking and handing over keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of cases with findings to record.
research_questions: Are positioning injuries recorded more completely?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few findings; high: long procedures with frequent findings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
